# The Healthcare AP Automation Benchmark Report: Summer 2026 Edition


**by Mike Waldron**


## Why This Report Exists


Healthcare finance teams are operating under a different kind of pressure than most back-office functions. A Director of Finance managing AP across 40 locations isn’t just processing invoices; they’re doing it inside multi-entity GL structures, with regulatory reporting requirements that don’t bend for a busy month. A vendor invoice that goes unpaid isn’t just a billing problem. It can mean a medical supply delivery gets held, or a waste management vendor stops showing up, and that’s a care delivery problem.


Most operators know there’s exposure somewhere in their AP process. What they don’t have is the data to quantify it, to know exactly how much fraud risk is sitting in their invoice queue, or how many hours their team is losing to double-entry between their AP tool and a clinical system. That gap between sensing a problem and proving it is where healthcare AP has always struggled.


We process hundreds of thousands of invoices across our healthcare customer base. This report is what the data actually show: not industry estimates or survey responses, but numbers pulled from real operations.


This is the first edition. Twice a year, we’ll track how these numbers change, flag what’s driving the changes, and provide healthcare finance teams with a benchmark they can actually use. This edition covers duplicate detection, fraud exposure, payment errors, invoice lifecycle time, and AP labor savings.


## Profitability Benchmarks


### Duplicate Detection


**Benchmark** : Healthcare accounts save an average of $1.4 million per year from duplicate detection. Each caught duplicate is worth roughly $1,300 on average.


In Q2 2026 alone, healthcare customers saved an average of $450,000 per account, on pace for $1.8 million this year. Each caught duplicate averaged $1,440.


Duplicate invoices are among the most common and preventable sources of AP loss. For organizations running AP across multiple communities or facilities, this isn’t a minor catch. It’s over $1 million a year disappearing if nobody flags it automatically.


### Invoice Risk


**Benchmark** : 42 percent of healthcare organizations reported experiencing invoice fraud or overpayment in the past year.


So far in 2026, 76 percent of healthcare accounts had at least one invoice flagged for potential risk. The average flagged invoice carried $2,494 in exposure.


At scale, invoice fraud isn’t rare. It’s close to a certainty. With three in four accounts flagging at least one risky invoice this year, the real question for any healthcare finance team isn’t whether fraud or overpayment will show up in the queue. It’s whether it gets caught before the check goes out.


### Payments


**Benchmark** : Ottimate caught 14,250 payments with errors last year, accounting for $1.6 million in potential losses.


So far this year, Ottimate has caught 6,026 payments with errors, accounting for $1.01 million in potential losses.


Payment errors are expensive and hard to recover once funds leave the account. Halfway through the year, healthcare accounts are already closing in on last year’s full total. Manual payment reviews miss what automated checks catch consistently, which is exactly why a final validation layer before disbursement matters.


## Productivity Benchmarks


### Invoice Lifecycle Time


**Benchmark** : Healthcare customers have reduced invoice lifecycle time, from upload to coding to approval, from 11 days to 4.4 days, saving the average account $82,000 per year in AP labor. 31 percent of healthcare invoices were approved in under 24 hours over the past year.


These numbers have held steady throughout 2026.


An 11-day invoice cycle isn’t just slow. It shows up in late fees, strained vendor relationships, and staff hours that never get recovered. For operators managing dozens of vendors across multiple communities or facilities, faster approvals aren’t a convenience. They’re a measurable bottom-line impact, and a way to protect the vendor relationships that medical supply and care delivery depend on.


### AP Labor Savings


**Benchmark** : Ottimate healthcare customers have 94.3 percent of invoice line items GL-coded correctly on first pass, no manual rework needed, saving an average of 147 hours and $7,400 per month in AP coding labor.


So far in 2026, Ottimate healthcare customers have 93.7 percent of invoice line items GL-coded correctly on first pass, with similar savings realized.


Manual GL coding, especially when it means re-keying data into a clinical system after it’s already been coded elsewhere, is one of the most time-consuming and error-prone parts of AP. Getting it right more than nine times out of ten on the first pass means less double-entry and more time for the work that actually requires judgment. As invoice volume grows, that efficiency gap only widens.


## About This Report


The Healthcare AP Automation Benchmark Report: Summer 2026 Edition is published by Ottimate using aggregated, anonymized data from our healthcare customer base. All benchmarks reflect real invoice processing data across senior living, assisted living, and other healthcare operators. This is the first edition; future editions will track trends and flag what’s driving the changes.
